questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to and English speaking country as well as a place I'd never been before. Furthermore, I chose University of Melbourne because of its interesting subjects and good reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None... I accidentally booked the pickup from the airport to the wrong date and was denied access to the vehicle even though my friends that I was going to stay with got in and there were plenty of space.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy but very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to live at Unilodge Lincoln House you should book via their own website - not though the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was extremely expensive to live close to campus. I payed around 7500 DKK per month to stay at a small dorm room with shared facilities.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When I arrived I went to orientation where I got all of the instructions on how to register properly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student support worked very well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered as soon as the system allowed me to, hence I got all the subjects I wanted with very few clashes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possible and plan from home. Also have a few back-ups approved from both University of Copenhagen and University of Melbourne. I ended of changing one of mine after classes started as I did not like the one I originally chose. It was very easy because I had gotten my back-up approved beforehand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did one first year as my "for fun" elective (Australia in the Wine World). Two second year subjects and one third year. The subjects were definitely not too hard - nor too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At University of Melbourne they gave me a lot of tests and other assignments to complete during the semester. These accounted for part of my final grade. I really liked this style of teaching as it took part of the pressure away from the final exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039)
Pharmacology: How Drugs Work
Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration
Plant Biodiversity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would in particular recommend Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration if you are interested in Stem Cells. It is a very interesting and well structured subject that gives both a lot of information about the basics and the newer research within the stem cell field.

I also really liked Plant Biodiversity as it gave a good insight in Australia's flora. Australia in the Wine World was also a lot of fun with weekly wine tastings and lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy my own Pans, pots, duvet, pillow etc on my student accommodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a bit more expensive than expected. But I didn't have to buy any books for university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There a so many clubs and societies. Sports, languages, food, arts, and music just to name some.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the Sexpression and the Swifties societies. They were a lot of fun to be part of. I also joined the gym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Great Ocean Road, Dandenong Ranges, Phillip Island, Grampians, wine districts (all for a day- or weekend trip). Sydney, Brisbane, Tasmania, Gold Coast are for holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. There are also a lot of other exchange students from all over the world.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to unimelb's events for exchange student, attend orientation week, and if you live a Unilodge Lincoln House then go so some of their events too.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular. The Australians are not that different from Danes and they are very nice and welcoming people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very easy to talk to and will help you with anything if needed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to travel around and see some of Australia's nature - also during the weekend. Plan which subjects you want to enroll in before you go. Go the the socializing events in the start of the semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and traveling Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period was pretty though as I had three exams in three days.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
